pages.title: Authentication and MDS auth caps (cephx, MDSAuthCaps, root_squash, fsname/path restrictions)

features.name: cephx authentication of peers connecting to the MDS
features.description: Incoming msgr2/msgr1 connections present a cephx authorizer for service type MDS. MonClient (as AuthServer) verifies it with the rotating mds service secret, then MDSDaemon::ms_handle_fast_authentication parses the caps blob (no mds_lock); failure refuses the connection with -EACCES (AUTH_BAD_METHOD). ms_handle_accept then attaches/creates a Session and stores the parsed MDSAuthCaps.
features.notes: An entity without any mds cap has an empty caps blob; decoding fails and the connection is refused. Caps are parsed in ms_handle_accept; a msgr2 reconnect merged into an existing Connection (ProtocolV2::reuse_connection, src/msg/async/ProtocolV2.cc:2814) does not copy the newly verified peer_caps_info, so caps change only with a new Connection object (code reading). RotatingKeyRing::get_service_secret rejects a service_id other than MDS and secret_ids outside the three held secrets.

features.name: MDS self-authentication (keyring, rotating mds service secrets, service tickets for mon/osd/mds/mgr)
features.description: MDSDaemon::init sets want_keys MON|OSD|MDS|MGR, installs MonClient as messenger AuthClient and AuthServer, authenticates to the monitors and waits for rotating mds service secrets (rotating_keys_bootstrap_timeout x max_rotating_auth_attempts) before it can verify client authorizers; failure -> suicide. Default keyring for MDS daemons is $mds_data/keyring = /var/lib/ceph/mds/$cluster-$id/keyring (common_preinit), not the generic /etc/ceph list. The mon delivers three rotating secrets (prev/current/next); renewal when fewer than three are held or the current one expired at least min(30s, auth_service_ticket_ttl/4) ago.
features.notes: MDS entity caps as deployed: mon 'profile mds' (cephadm) or 'allow profile mds' (vstart, doc), osd 'allow rw tag cephfs *=*', mds 'allow' (required: peer MDSs refuse connections whose mds caps are missing or unparseable). mgr 'allow profile mds' appears only in vstart and doc/cephfs/add-remove-mds.rst:90 and is not needed: DaemonServer does no cap check on MMgrOpen/MMgrReport (src/mgr/DaemonServer.cc:601, 774). cephadm writes the keyring into the daemon data dir mounted at /var/lib/ceph/mds/ceph-<id>.

features.name: auth_none means allow-all
features.description: With auth_service_required=none the AuthNone handler sets AuthCapsInfo.allow_all=true and MDSDaemon::parse_caps calls set_allow_all(): every client is 'allow *', including tell commands.
features.notes: cephx tickets with allow_all=true are rejected by cephx_verify_authorizer.

features.name: MDS cap string grammar and parser
features.description: Boost.Spirit grammar: grants 'allow <spec> [fsname=F] [path=P] [root_squash] [uid=N] [gids=a,b] [network CIDR]' separated by ',' or ';'. spec is '*', 'all' or 'r' followed by optional w f p Q q s in that order. Qualifier order is fixed. Exact string 'allow' == 'allow rwps'. Also used by the monitor to validate caps.
features.notes: uid=0 is stored as 'any uid'. Unquoted path charset [a-zA-Z0-9_./-]. fsname charset [a-zA-Z0-9_.-]. Paths: leading '/' stripped; no '//', '.', '..' normalization. The legacy special case is a byte-exact compare: ' allow' and 'allow ' are rejected, while leading/trailing ascii::space around other strings is skipped by phrase_parse (verified by compiling the grammar verbatim against Boost 1.83). Separators allow only spaces around ','/';'. uid values >= 2^31 parse but never match (caller uid compared as int). Error text 'Permission flags ...' only when the unconsumed remainder contains 'allow', otherwise 'mds capability parse failed, stopped at ...'.

features.name: Grant evaluation MDSAuthCaps::is_capable (union of grants)
features.description: For each grant in order: network filter, fs/uid/gids/path match, r/w spec check, quarantine early deny, root_squash skip, p/s/f flag checks, then allow if uid is ANY, else chown/chgrp rules and owner/group/other mode-bit check. First passing grant allows; no grant -> false (-EACCES).
features.notes: Only the quarantine step can deny before later grants are consulted.

features.name: path= restriction
features.description: Grant applies only to inodes whose primary path (projected, from root, without leading '/') equals the grant path or continues with '/'. Empty path or '/' matches the whole fs. Also checked at session open against the client-claimed mount root (path_capable).
features.notes: Path restriction protects metadata only; data access is governed by OSD caps.

features.name: fsname= restriction and fs-name gating of sessions
features.description: Grants with fsname apply only to that filesystem ('' or '*' = any). Every MClientSession is rejected (CEPH_SESSION_REJECT, error_string 'client doesn't have caps for FS "<fs>"') and MClientReclaim silently dropped unless some grant for this fs allows read.
features.notes: Reconnect (MClientReconnect) does not re-check the fs name. fs rename does not rewrite caps.

features.name: uid=/gids= restriction with simplified mode-bit check
features.description: uid-restricted grants require caller_uid == uid (and a caller group in gids if gids given) and then check the owner, group (grant-listed gids only) or other permission bits of the target inode against MAY_READ/MAY_WRITE; chown only to self from self; chgrp only by owner to a listed group.
features.notes: Uses committed (non-projected) uid/gid/mode. O_WRONLY opens and stat need the read bit. Caller ids are client-asserted. MAY_CHOWN is only requested when the uid actually changes (Server.cc:5621), but a uid= grant requires new_uid == caller_uid == inode_uid, so chown is never allowed by a uid= grant. O_TRUNC opens check only MAY_WRITE.

features.name: root_squash
features.description: A root_squash grant cannot be used for requests whose mask contains MAY_WRITE when caller uid==0 or gid==0; other grants may still allow. Client-side enforcement via cap_auths for cached operations.
features.notes: Vxattr operations (mask MAY_SET_VXATTR only) are not squashed. fs authorize can add but not remove root_squash.

features.name: p flag (MAY_SET_VXATTR): layouts, quotas, pins, subvolume and other ceph.* vxattrs
features.description: Required for SETXATTR/RMXATTR of ceph.dir.layout*, ceph.file.layout*, ceph.quota*, ceph.quiesce.block, ceph.dir.subvolume(.snaps.visible), ceph.dir.pin(.random/.distributed), ceph.dir.charmap/normalization/encoding/casesensitive; for SETLAYOUT/SETDIRLAYOUT that change the layout; for CREATE with a non-inherited layout.
features.notes: setvxattr requests only MAY_SET_VXATTR (no MAY_WRITE), so 'allow rp' can set quotas/layouts.

features.name: s flag (MAY_SNAPSHOT): mksnap, rmsnap, renamesnap
features.description: Snapshot creation/removal/rename require MAY_WRITE|MAY_SNAPSHOT on the directory, after a caller uid range check against mds_snap_min_uid/mds_snap_max_uid (-EPERM).
features.notes: lssnap/snapdiff need only MAY_READ; SNAP_METADATA has no caps check.

features.name: f flag (MAY_FULL): bypass of metadata-pool-full ENOSPC
features.description: When the metadata pool has FLAG_FULL, SETLAYOUT, SETDIRLAYOUT, RMXATTR, SETXATTR, CREATE, SYMLINK, MKSNAP and first-pass LINK/RENAME proceed only if a grant with 'f' (or '*') passes check_access(MAY_FULL) on the request's base inode. On failure Server::check_access has already replied -EACCES and finished the request; dispatch_client_request then calls respond_to_request(-ENOSPC) again, sending a second MClientReply for the same tid that clients drop (kclient: 'unknown tid'). Clients therefore observe -EACCES, not the intended -ENOSPC (code reading).
features.notes: MKDIR/MKNOD are not gated; ceph fs authorize does not accept 'f'.

features.name: q/Q quarantine access flags
features.description: For quarantine-aware clients, check_access on quarantined inodes denies (-EACCES) at the first matching grant lacking q/Q; Locker restricts issued caps on quarantined inodes to PIN for sessions without q/Q under the inode path. Q and q are evaluated identically in code. Never implied by '*'.
features.notes: Details belong to the quarantine page.

features.name: network restriction
features.description: 'allow ... network A/P' grants apply only if the session's peer socket address is inside the CIDR (same address family); an unparsable network makes the grant unusable in is_capable.
features.notes: Ignored by allow_all(), fs_name_capable(), path_capable(); dropped by MDSAuthCaps::to_string (fs authorize merges). The grammar accepts '[' and ']' but parse_network uses inet_pton on 'addr/prefix', so a bracketed IPv6 network makes the grant unusable.

features.name: allow * gate for tell commands
features.description: MCommand (ceph tell mds.X, mgr commands) is executed only if the connection's caps satisfy allow_all() (a '*'/'all' grant with no path and no uid); otherwise MCommandReply(-EACCES, 'permission denied').
features.notes: allow_all() ignores fsname and network. Works without a rank (standby daemons).

features.name: fscrypt attribute changes require allow *
features.description: SETATTR with CEPH_SETATTR_FSCRYPT_AUTH or CEPH_SETATTR_FSCRYPT_FILE returns -EACCES unless the session caps satisfy allow_all().
features.notes: fscrypt_auth supplied at inode creation is copied without this gate (Server::prepare_new_inode).

features.name: Mount root validation at session open
features.description: Client metadata 'root' must start with '/' and be path_capable; otherwise CEPH_SESSION_REJECT 'invalue root' / 'non-allowable root' and a clog warning.
features.notes: Checked only when the client metadata contains a 'root' key (libcephfs omits it for mds_command on an unmounted client and start_reclaim, src/client/Client.cc:6897, 18885); the test is a textual prefix match ('/a/../b' passes path=/a). kclient sends server_path or '/'; REJECT makes kclient requests fail with -EACCES, libcephfs with -EPERM.

features.name: Session reclaim requires identical auth_name
features.description: MClientReclaim of a session by uuid is refused with -EPERM if the reclaiming session's cephx entity name differs from the target's; auth_name is persisted in session_info_t and ESession for this purpose.
features.notes: Used by NFS-Ganesha HA restarts.

features.name: cap_auths export in CEPH_SESSION_OPEN
features.description: Each OPEN reply carries vector<MDSCapAuth> (match fields + readable + writeable) in grant order; sent from _session_logged, the already-open re-notification (REQUEST_OPEN with NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE on an open session), finish_force_open_sessions (subtree import, rejoin, cross-MDS rename) and reconnect. Only present when the message is encoded v>=6 (metadata or supported_features non-empty; the MDS fills supported_features only for CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC clients).
features.notes: kclient decodes positionally ignoring struct_len; layout is a hard contract.

features.name: CEPHFS_FEATURE_MDS_AUTH_CAPS_CHECK and MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH health
features.description: Sessions with root_squash caps whose client lacks feature bit 21 (client_mds_auth_caps) are recorded in SessionMap::broken_root_squash_clients (not rejected); Beacon reports HEALTH_ERR MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH per client or summarized above mds_health_summarize_threshold.
features.notes: Admins can require the feature via fs required_client_features (sessions lacking it are evicted). The set stores raw Session pointers and is erased only in SessionMap::remove_session; a session rejected after insertion (bad root, duplicate uuid) leaves a dangling pointer once ms_handle_reset drops the bootstrap session, which notify_health would dereference (code reading).

features.name: Per-request check_access matrix
features.description: 28 call sites in Server.cc request specific masks on specific inodes (target for getattr/open/setattr/xattr/readdir, parent dir for create/mknod/mkdir/symlink/unlink, src+dst dirs and source inode for rename, target+dst dir for link). Unchecked: RMXATTR of non-ceph names, GETVXATTR, SETFILELOCK/GETFILELOCK, FILE_BLOCKDIFF, SNAP_METADATA.
features.notes: Link/unlink/rename checks run only before peers have witnessed. lookup_ino uses mask 0 (path test only).

features.name: stray_prior_path-based authorization of unlinked inodes
features.description: For inodes whose parent is a stray directory, the path used for auth is the inode's stray_prior_path (set at unlink/rename-over); for inodes inside a deleted snapshotted dir, the parent's stray_prior_path.
features.notes: Open-unlinked files must stay accessible to path-restricted clients.

features.name: Snapshot uid range mds_snap_min_uid/mds_snap_max_uid
features.description: mksnap, rmsnap, renamesnap and snap metadata ops return -EPERM if caller_uid is outside [mds_snap_min_uid (0), mds_snap_max_uid (4294967294)].

features.name: FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 check
features.description: check_access returns -EIO for directories whose layout has a pool namespace when the client connection lacks CEPH_FEATURE_FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2.
features.notes: Legacy clients only.

features.name: Batched getattr/lookup share the head's access decision
features.description: With mds_allow_batched_ops (default true), followers of a getattr/lookup batch receive the head's result code and trace without their own check_access, across sessions.
features.notes: Batches are keyed by inode/dentry and getattr mask, not by session.

features.name: Peer-type message filtering and MDS address check
features.description: ALLOW_MESSAGES_FROM restricts daemon/rank messages by connection peer type (MON, MDS, OSD, CLIENT); messages claiming to come from an MDS rank must arrive on the connection to that rank's MDSMap address (is_stale_message). MDS never forwards client requests itself.
features.notes: MSG_COMMAND is not type-filtered; it is gated by allow_all(). On the accepting side ProtocolV2::handle_hello takes the peer type from HELLO and the message source is entity_name_t(HELLO type, CLIENT_IDENT gid); no comparison with the authenticated EntityName/global_id was found (code search). Requests from non-client types get no Session, and check_access is a no-op for session-less requests.

features.name: ceph fs authorize cap generation and merge
features.description: Monitor generates mon 'allow r[ fsname=F]', mds 'allow <perm>[ fsname=F][ path=P][ root_squash]' per pair and osd 'allow r[w] tag cephfs data=<fs>'; validates with MDSAuthCaps::parse; merges into existing caps by (fs_name, path): spec replaced, root_squash only added; merged string from to_string() drops network and quotes.
features.notes: Perm flags must be ASCII-ordered except leading 'rw' (so rp, rq, rQ and rf are rejected by ordering; f after rw is 'Unknown permission flag'); rs is accepted. If merging hits CAPS_PARSING_ERR the handler jumps to done with err 0 (success reported, nothing changed; src/mon/AuthMonitor.cc:2021).

features.name: mgr/volumes subvolume authorize/deauthorize/evict
features.description: fs subvolume authorize creates/updates client.<auth_id> with mds 'allow r|rw path=<subvol path>' (no fsname), osd 'allow r|rw pool=<pool>[ namespace=<ns>]', mon 'allow r'; bookkeeping in /volumes/$<auth_id>.meta and /volumes/_<group>:<subvol>.meta under libcephfs flock; evict uses 'session evict auth_name=<id> client_metadata.root=<path>' on all up ranks.
features.notes: Rust MDS must support session evict filters auth_name and client_metadata.root, and flock via libcephfs.

features.name: mgr/nfs export user caps
features.description: Ganesha FSAL users get mds 'allow rw path=<export path>', osd 'allow rw pool=<nfs pool> namespace=<cluster>, allow rw tag cephfs data=<fs>', mon 'allow r'; access type and squash enforced by Ganesha.

features.name: Daemon key rotation via tell rotate-key
features.description: The MDS accepts 'ceph tell mds.<name> rotate-key -i <key>' in the MonClient asok hook (adds the key for its own entity to the in-memory keyring); mon side uses 'auth get-or-create-pending' / 'auth commit-pending'. cephadm's _rotate_daemon_key (pending key, keyring rewrite, rotate-key tell, restart fallback) has no caller at this commit: 'ceph orch daemon rotate-key' raises 'key rotation by orchestrator not supported in this release'.
features.notes: Tell is subject to the allow * gate.

features.name: Required client features eviction (e.g. client_mds_auth_caps)
features.description: When fs required_client_features changes, open sessions lacking a required feature are evicted (blocklisted per mds_session_blocklist_on_evict); new sessions are rejected with 'missing required features'.

features.name: POSIX DAC enforced by clients, not by the MDS
features.description: The MDS never requests MAY_EXECUTE and has no ACL/sticky-bit logic; mode/ACL permission checks are done by kclient (generic_permission) and libcephfs (client_permissions, client_acl_type).
features.notes: An MDS-side DAC check would be new behavior, not C++ parity.

features.name: Caps not refreshed on msgr2 reconnect
features.description: Client connections use the stateful_server policy; a reconnect is merged into the existing Connection by ProtocolV2::reuse_connection, which moves auth_meta and the socket but not peer_caps_info. send_reconnect_ok queues ms_handle_accept, which re-parses the caps already stored on the existing Connection. New caps apply only to a newly accepted Connection object.
features.notes: Code reading; not reproduced. mgr/nfs works around non-refreshing caps by always granting allow rw path=<export>.

serialization_points.name: Incoming connection authentication under monc_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: MonClient rotating secrets, auth handler registry, MonClient state
serialization_points.why_serialized: MonClient protects all of its state with one mutex; authorizer decryption and the MDS caps parse (ms_handle_fast_authentication) run while holding it
serialization_points.notes: Verification is a pure function of the read-mostly rotating keyring (three secrets) and the caps string; ms_handle_fast_authentication runs inside monc_lock without mds_lock.

serialization_points.name: Session attach and caps parse in ms_handle_accept
serialization_points.shared_state: SessionMap lookup, Session::auth_caps, Session connection and preopen_out_queue

serialization_points.name: Session open gating and ESession journaling
serialization_points.shared_state: session state, SessionMap projected version, MDLog
serialization_points.why_serialized: runs in the mds_lock dispatch path; ESession is appended to the rank journal
serialization_points.notes: Auth checks themselves are per-session; journal ordering is per log stream.

serialization_points.name: Inode path construction for every check_access
serialization_points.shared_state: projected parent dentries of all ancestors up to the root, inode uid/gid/mode, session caps
serialization_points.why_serialized: path built by walking cache parents under mds_lock; a concurrent rename of any ancestor would change the result
serialization_points.notes: Needs a consistent view of ancestor names only; a per-subtree root path plus relative path removes the global dependency.

serialization_points.name: Quarantine caps evaluation on every cap issue
serialization_points.why_serialized: under mds_lock; builds the inode path string unconditionally for every issue_caps/issue_new_caps
serialization_points.notes: Cost exists even when nothing is quarantined. The same make_path_string + quarantine_access_in_caps happens in CInode::try_drop_loner, get_xlocker_mask, get_caps_allowed_for_client and encode_inodestat (src/mds/CInode.cc:3490, 3788, 3807, 4199).

serialization_points.name: Tell command allow_all gate
serialization_points.shared_state: session caps of the command connection
serialization_points.why_serialized: every message goes through MDSDaemon::ms_dispatch2 which takes mds_lock

serialization_points.name: broken_root_squash_clients set
serialization_points.shared_state: rank-global set of Session pointers read by Beacon::notify_health
serialization_points.why_serialized: mutated under mds_lock, read under mds_lock plus Beacon::mutex

serialization_points.name: Batched getattr/lookup
serialization_points.shared_state: CInode/CDentry batch_ops map, batch head result
serialization_points.why_serialized: followers wait for the head and reuse its result (including its access decision)
serialization_points.notes: Access decision should be per session.

serialization_points.name: Rotating secret renewal
serialization_points.notes: Key material is shared but read-mostly.

external_contract.detail: kclient authenticates with a ticket for CEPH_ENTITY_TYPE_MDS (msgr1 and msgr2 callbacks), supports authorizer challenges; on AUTH_BAD_METHOD it invalidates the ticket, revalidates with the mon and returns -EACCES.
REQUEST_OPEN metadata 'root' = mount server_path or '/'; must start with '/' and be path_capable or the session is rejected. The MDS checks the root only if the key is present, textually.
REJECT moves the session to REJECTED; subsequent requests fail with -EACCES unless recover_session=clean.

Decoded when msg_version >= 6 and op == OPEN; per element: skip 6-byte MDSCapAuth header, skip 6-byte MDSCapMatch header, s64 uid, u32 n + n x u32 gids, u32+bytes path (trailing '/' stripped), u32+bytes fs_name, u8 root_squash, u8 readable, u8 writeable. Replaces the mount-wide list on every OPEN.

ceph_mds_check_access before ceph_open, ceph_atomic_open (parent dir path), ceph_unlink/rmdir/rmsnap, __ceph_setattr; last matching grant decides r/w/root_squash; no match = allow; returns -EACCES locally.
Advertised in session open supported_features; absence with root_squash caps triggers MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH.
caller_uid/caller_gid = fsuid/fsgid, owner_uid/owner_gid for new-inode ops (idmapped mounts), full supplementary gid list as u64 values (v4 tail).
REJECT error_string is logged and pending operations/mount fail with -EPERM.
Client::mds_check_access with MDSCapMatch::match semantics, last matching grant wins; used in _do_setattr and in cap-satisfied _open.
FSAL users carry mds 'allow rw path=<export>'; LOOKUPINO by handle is constrained by the mask-0 path test; reclaim requires identical auth_name.
AuthCapsInfo{allow_all=false, caps=one encoded std::string with the entity's mds caps}; cephx never sets allow_all; extra trailing bytes rejected.

external_contract.item: MDS cap string validation and generation
external_contract.detail: The monitor validates mds caps with MDSAuthCaps::parse (mon_auth_validate_all_caps) and generates/merges them for fs authorize using MDSAuthCaps::merge/to_string; a Rust MDS must parse every string the mon accepts.
Beacons and offload targets require 'mds' X; client eviction uses 'osd blocklist'; snap removal uses 'osd pool rmsnap' (profile mds).

The MDS must fetch and renew rotating secrets for its service type to verify client authorizers; startup waits rotating_keys_bootstrap_timeout x max_rotating_auth_attempts. The monitor delivers three secrets (prev/current/next); the MDS renews when fewer than three are held or the current one expired at least min(30s, auth_service_ticket_ttl/4) ago; tickets verify only while their secret_id is among the held three (no expires check).
mgr (mds 'allow *') sends MCommand; non-allow-all callers get -EACCES 'permission denied'.
Generates 'allow r|rw path=<subvol>' (no fsname); evicts with session evict filters auth_name and client_metadata.root.
HEALTH_ERR metric per client (metadata client_id) or summarized (client_count) via beacon.

Not active at this commit: _rotate_daemon_key has no caller and 'ceph orch daemon rotate-key' raises 'key rotation by orchestrator not supported in this release'. Manual flow: 'auth get-or-create-pending', then 'ceph tell mds.<name> rotate-key -i <key>' (MonClient asok hook), then 'auth commit-pending'.
MDS entity uses osd 'allow rw tag cephfs *=*'; OSDs evaluate it for every MDS op.

external_contract.item: client data access independent of MDS caps
external_contract.detail: MDS path restrictions do not protect file data; clients need matching OSD caps (pool/namespace).

-EACCES caps denial/fscrypt/tell, and also the first reply when the metadata pool is full and no f grant matches (a duplicate -ENOSPC reply follows and is dropped by clients); -EPERM snapshot uid range and reclaim auth_name mismatch; -ENOSPC for growing SETATTR while full; -EIO pool-namespace layout to old clients.

MgrClient MMgrOpen/MMgrReport are accepted without any cap check and the mgr accepts connections with empty mgr caps; cephadm grants the MDS no mgr cap, vstart and the manual-deploy doc grant 'allow profile mds'.
For MDS daemons the default keyring option is $mds_data/keyring (/var/lib/ceph/mds/$cluster-$id/keyring); key/keyfile options override. cephadm writes the keyring there via the data-dir bind mount.

rust_implications.implication: Implement the exact Spirit grammar including quirks (fixed flag and qualifier order, uid=0 means any, legacy 'allow' = rwps, unquoted path charset, network with space, ',' or ';' separators) and reuse src/test/mds/TestMDSAuthCaps.cc vectors as golden tests; the monitor validates with the C++ parser, so anything it accepts must be accepted. Include the byte-exact legacy 'allow' special case (' allow' and 'allow ' rejected), ascii::space pre/post-skip, and the int-typed uid comparison (uid >= 2^31 never matches) if bit-for-bit parity is wanted.

A drop-in MDS needs a full cephx service implementation: MonClient authentication with the MDS keyring, rotating mds service secrets, authorizer verification (incl. challenge round), msgr2 auth frames and crc/secure modes, and refusal of connections whose mds caps are missing or unparseable.

is_capable is a pure function of (immutable per-connection caps snapshot, inode path, committed uid/gid/mode, caller creds, mask, peer address); store caps per session as an immutable Arc and evaluate on worker threads without any global lock.

rust_implications.topic: Path computation in a sharded design
rust_implications.implication: Path grants need the inode's absolute primary path. Give each shard/subtree a cached absolute root path and evaluate relative paths inside it; invalidate cached prefixes on ancestor renames (cross-shard 2PC renames must bump a path epoch).

mgr/volumes caps 'allow r|rw path=<subvol path>' confine a session to one subvolume; the grant set can be used to bind sessions to subvolume shards for per-subvolume QoS, metrics and recovery without per-request lookups.

Send cap_auths (exact v1 MDSCapAuth/MDSCapMatch layout, grant order preserved, path without leading '/') in every CEPH_SESSION_OPEN including force-open/import and reconnect; never send an empty list for a restricted session (C++ can for imported sessions before the client connects).
Clients apply last-matching-grant semantics and allow when nothing matches; keep MDS union semantics for parity, and be aware that async create/unlink results depend on both agreeing.

C++ does not check caps for RMXATTR (non-ceph names), GETVXATTR, file locks, FILE_BLOCKDIFF and SNAP_METADATA; decide explicitly whether to replicate (parity) or add checks (stricter, observable EACCES differences).
If getattr/lookup batching or result sharing is implemented, run the access check per session; C++ shares the head's decision across sessions.
Caps are derived from the live connection, so per-shard journals and parallel replay need no auth data; only auth_name per session must be persisted (reclaim).

Implement CEPHFS_FEATURE_MDS_AUTH_CAPS_CHECK detection and the MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH health metric, keyed by a per-session flag instead of a raw-pointer set (C++ can leave dangling entries); check the kclient feature-bit layout (bit 22 is SUBVOLUME_METRICS in the 7.3-rc6+ kclient snapshot af32da41b03 but CHARMAP in the C++ MDS) before choosing the Rust feature bitset.
Tell commands and fscrypt setattr require allow_all() which ignores fsname and network; keep for compatibility (mgr relies on mds 'allow *'), or document any tightening.

The f flag needs the metadata pool FLAG_FULL bit from the latest OSDMap available to every worker (atomic snapshot), and the same op list (MKDIR/MKNOD excluded). Decide explicitly between the C++ observable result (-EACCES first reply, duplicate -ENOSPC dropped) and the intended -ENOSPC; never send two replies for one tid.
C++ uses committed uid/gid/mode and projected paths without extra locks; a Rust lock manager can read these from an MVCC snapshot instead of taking inode locks for authorization.

Derive peer type and client id from the authenticated ticket (EntityName type, global_id) rather than from HELLO/CLIENT_IDENT; the C++ MDS relies on HELLO-derived values for message filtering and for deciding whether a request gets a session (and therefore any caps check).

C++ keeps the old caps across msgr2 reconnects into an existing connection; refreshing caps on every successful AUTH would be stricter and observable (a client could lose access on reconnect). Document the chosen behavior.
